source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Mention the date and time of the inspection.
3. Identify the building/ property name and address for reference.
4. Describe the general purpose of the building (residential, commercial, educational etc.)
5. Note the standards or regulations used as the benchmark for the inspection (e.g., Americans with Disabilities Act - ADA, ICC/ANSI A117.1, local city ordinance).
6. Record the specific accessibility features inspected (e.g., ramps, elevators, restrooms, signage, parking, width of doorways, Braille instructions, fittings, etc.).
7. For each feature:
   - Take photos or drawings as visual evidence of the failed check.
   - Describe the specifications & measurements of the features in detail (such as dimensions, slopes, heights, etc.).
   - Indicate the requirement or standard it failed to meet (e.g., ADA requires 36-inch doorways but found a 32-inch doorway).
